rationales: The K shell is the first shell, not the M shell.
The L shell is the second shell, not the M shell.
The M shell has principal quantum number 3 and contains three subshells.
The N shell has principal quantum number 4, not 3.
Chlorine is a gas at room temperature.
Bromine is the halogen that is liquid at room temperature.
Fluorine is a gas at room temperature.
Iodine is a solid at room temperature.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass here, so it diffuses fastest.
Helium is heavier than hydrogen and therefore diffuses more slowly.
Fluorine is much heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Chlorine is the heaviest option and diffuses most slowly.
Honey is denser than water and settles when placed beneath it.
Kerosene oil floats on water because it is less dense.
Benzene is less dense than water and floats on it.
NaCl dissolves in water rather than settling as an insoluble substance.
Strontium isotopes can be produced in uranium-235 fission, but the question gives no isotope mass number.
Cobalt is not the expected fission-product choice in the usual examples.
Barium isotopes can also be produced in uranium-235 fission, so this is another plausible choice.
Arsenic is not the expected fission-product choice in the usual examples.
Removing electrons leaves a negatively charged anion, not a positively charged ion.
Electron removal alone does not necessarily form a molecule.
A molecular ion is a charged molecule, not the general result of removing electrons from an atom.
Removing negatively charged electrons leaves the atom positively charged, forming a cation.
The boron family does not have an outer configuration of ns¹.
The boron family does not have an outer configuration of ns² alone.
The configuration ns²np² characterizes the carbon family.
Boron-family elements have the general outer configuration ns²np¹.
17.5 mmHg is approximately the vapor pressure of water at 20°C, not 40°C.
149.4 mmHg is much higher than the vapor pressure at 40°C.
Water’s vapor pressure at 40°C is about 55.3 mmHg.

N₂ has complete octets for both nitrogen atoms.
O₂ has complete octets for both oxygen atoms.
Ionic bonds typically form through electron transfer, often between a metal and a nonmetal.
Two nonmetals generally share electrons and form a covalent bond.
A coordinate covalent bond is a particular covalent bond formed when one atom supplies both shared electrons, not the general expected answer.
Metallic bonding occurs among metal atoms, not between two nonmetals.
At equal solution volume, a 1 M solution has less water than a more dilute solution.
At equal solution volume, a 2 M solution has less water than a more dilute solution.
The 0.25 M solution is the most dilute and therefore contains the most water for an equal volume.
The 0.5 M solution is more concentrated than 0.25 M and contains less water for an equal volume.
Grams of solute per 100 cm³ of solution is percent mass/volume (% m/v).
Percent mass/mass uses grams of solute per 100 g of solution.
Percent volume/mass uses volume of solute per mass of solution.
Percent volume/volume uses volume of solute per volume of solution.

Zinc is a metal and is malleable.
Sulphur is a nonmetal and is brittle rather than malleable.
Phosphorus is a nonmetal and is not malleable.
